questions.question: The audio format MP3 stands for:
questions.explanation: MP3 stands for MPEG Layer 3.

questions.question: In automata theory, a class of languages is said to be closed under an operation when:

options.A: Applying it moves the result to a higher Chomsky type
options.B: Applying it to languages of the class gives a language of the same class
options.C: Applying it always produces the empty language
options.D: Applying it always produces a finite language

questions.explanation: Closure means taking languages from a class and performing the operation yields a language that belongs to the same class.

questions.concept: Tracing a WHILE loop that halves n
questions.question: Trace this pseudocode: INPUT n (n = 20); count = 0; WHILE n > 0: n = n DIV 2 (integer division), INCREMENT count; PRINT count. What is printed?
questions.explanation: n goes 20, 10, 5, 2, 1, 0, so the loop body runs 5 times and count = 5.

questions.question: Which process model supports iterative development and is commonly used by teams that deliver work in short iterations?
questions.explanation: The agile model supports iterative development; waterfall and the linear sequential model are non-iterative, and Build and Fix has no planned iterations.

questions.question: What is the result of applying the SQL scalar function UCASE() to the text 'dbms'?
questions.explanation: UCASE() converts a field to upper case; LEN() would return the length 4 and MID() would extract characters such as D.

questions.question: ROM is needed to store an initial program that starts the computer. This program is called the:
questions.explanation: ROM stores the bootstrap loader, which loads the operating system into memory at startup.

questions.concept: Flight simulator headset as Virtual Reality
questions.question: A trainee pilot wears a headset that places them inside a fully computer-generated three-dimensional cockpit and lets them explore it. Which technology is being used?
questions.explanation: VR is a three-dimensional, computer-generated situation that simulates the real world and uses VR headsets. AR only overlays information on the existing physical surroundings.

questions.question: Stealing the ideas or creations of others and presenting them as one's own is known as:
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is stealing the ideas or creations of others.

questions.concept: Waterfall unsuitable when requirements keep changing
questions.question: A client warns that the requirements of a project will change frequently while development is in progress. Which model is the poorest fit for this situation?
questions.explanation: The waterfall model is not suitable for accommodating changes because each phase is completed before the next begins; agile, prototyping and incremental models handle evolving requirements better.

questions.concept: sort() sorts in place and returns None
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
x = [3, 1, 2]
y = x.sort()
print(y)
questions.explanation: sort() sorts the list in place and returns None. sorted() is the function that returns a new sorted list.

questions.question: Which protocol establishes a dedicated, direct connection between two devices (such as a home computer to an ISP through a modem) and requires duplex-capable devices?
questions.explanation: PPP defines how two directly linked devices authenticate and exchange data, and requires duplex mode.

questions.question: Processes P1, P2 and P3 arrive at time 0 in that order with CPU bursts of 24 ms, 3 ms and 3 ms. What is the average waiting time under FCFS?
questions.explanation: Under FCFS the waiting times are P1 = 0, P2 = 24 and P3 = 27, so the average is 51 / 3 = 17 ms. 3 ms would be the SJF result.

questions.question: The function linearSearch(list, key) returns index + 1 when list[index] == key, and None otherwise. What does it return for list = [8, -4, 7, 17, 0, 2, 19] and key = 0?
questions.explanation: 0 is at index 4, and the function returns index + 1 = 5 (its position).

questions.concept: Paging removes external but may cause internal fragmentation
questions.question: Which statement about paging and fragmentation is correct?

options.A: Paging requires pages to be stored contiguously in memory
options.B: Paging removes external fragmentation but may cause internal fragmentation
options.C: Paging causes both internal and external fragmentation
options.D: Paging removes internal fragmentation but causes external fragmentation

questions.explanation: Because pages can be placed in any free frame, there is no external fragmentation; the last page of a process may not fill its frame, causing internal fragmentation.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
f = open('myfile.txt', 'a+')
print(f.mode)
questions.explanation: The mode attribute returns the access mode used to open the file. The closed attribute would return a Boolean.

questions.question: Which HTML code correctly changes the font face of text to Calibri?
questions.explanation: The face attribute of the font tag sets the typeface: <font face="Calibri">.

questions.concept: Lower sublayer of data link layer
questions.question: The Data Link layer is divided into two sublayers. Which one is the lower sublayer?
questions.explanation: The lower sublayer of the Data Link layer is MAC; LLC is the upper sublayer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a thick (fat) client application?
questions.explanation: Thick clients keep most logic on the device, e.g. MS Word, Outlook, Excel. Gmail, Office 365 and search engines are thin client examples.

questions.concept: Selection sort list after second pass
questions.question: Selection sort (ascending) is applied to [8, 7, 13, 1, -9, 4]. What is the list after the second pass?
questions.explanation: Pass 1 swaps 8 and -9 giving [-9, 7, 13, 1, 8, 4]. Pass 2 finds the minimum 1 in the unsorted part and swaps it with 7, giving [-9, 1, 13, 7, 8, 4].

questions.question: Who introduced the concept of a stored program computer, capable of storing both data and program in memory?
questions.explanation: John von Neumann introduced the stored program concept, on which EDVAC and ENIAC were based. Babbage designed the Analytical Engine and Pascal the Pascaline.

questions.question: In a Turing machine, what is the blank symbol used for?
questions.explanation: The blank symbol represents empty cells on the tape.

questions.concept: Sum of truncated casts in Java
questions.question:
What is the value of x after this Java statement?

int x = (int) 9.99 + (int) 2.5;
questions.explanation: Each cast truncates its own value: (int) 9.99 is 9 and (int) 2.5 is 2, so x = 11. Truncation discards the fraction; it does not round to 10 + 3 = 13.

questions.question: In which DBMS architecture is the database directly available to the user on the local system, with no network connection required?
questions.explanation: Single-tier architecture is a local database system used for local development and needs no network connection.

questions.question: Among compilers used for C++, GCC stands for:
questions.explanation: GCC is the GNU Compiler Collection, listed with Turbo C++, Dev C++, Borland C++ and Microsoft Visual C++.

questions.concept: Virus remains dormant until infected file is executed
questions.question: A user downloads an infected executable file but does not open it for a week. During that week, the virus in the file:

options.A: may stay dormant until the infected file is opened or executed
options.B: spreads by itself across the network like a worm
options.C: is removed automatically when the system restarts
options.D: encrypts the user's files and demands a ransom

questions.explanation: A virus may remain dormant until the infected file is opened or executed; self-propagation over a network is worm behaviour and demanding ransom is ransomware behaviour.
